item.title: The House Freedom Caucus has to transform — it could preview the GOP's post-Trump era
item.description:
President Trump announced last week that three news organizations—CNN, MS NOW, and Politico —would be banned from White House press briefings because they are “Fake News Media Outlets” publishing “one-sided,” “never good,” “purposely negative stories” about him. Over the weekend, reporters from those outlets were denied entry to the West Wing. On Monday the three organizations sued Trump, claiming the ban is unconstitutional. Now the rest of the press is chattering about the prospects of that suit. Take it to the bank: The media companies will win. My guess is that the district court will enjoin the ban within a week. Here’s why I’m so confident. The case was filed in the federal District Court for the District of Columbia. That court is required to follow decisions of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. item.title: Sri Lanka: 15 men jailed for life in 2019 Easter bombings
item.description:
Islamic State-inspired bombings of churches and hotels in 2019 was one of the country’s worst ever attacks A court in Sri Lanka has convicted 15 men on terrorist charges for their involvement in the deadly 2019 Easter bombings and sentenced them each to at least 220 years in prison. The terror attacks, which targeted luxury hotels and churches as they held Easter services, left 267 people dead and wounded almost 6000. The bombings, which were inspired by Islamic State (IS), were among the deadliest attacks in Sri Lanka’s history and sent shockwaves through the country. Continue reading...

item.title: Trump defends actions in Iran and Venezuela in UN General Assembly address amid rising tensions with allies – as it happened
item.description:
President Trump’s rambling, combative speech Tuesday to the United Nations General Assembly saw him return to his most serious quagmire yet—the war in Iran—telling world leaders that he was considering completely destroying the country as a means to end the conflict he launched alongside Israel in February. “Do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again? Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?” Trump pondered aloud, claiming that Iran’s leadership had rejected multiple peace deals with the US. He said little about the terms of those offers—and nothing about the US and Israel’s explosive role in the Middle East , from Iran and the Gulf to Gaza and beyond. item.title: EU drops sanctions for Russian oligarchs Usmanov and Fridman
item.description:
Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman delisted in what Ireland’s EU presidency calls ‘a difficult compromise’ for the bloc The EU has agreed to remove two Russian billionaires, Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, from its sanctions list, while extending restrictions on nearly 3,000 individuals and companies accused of supporting the war on Ukraine for the next three years. With an end-of-Tuesday deadline looming to preserve the Russia blacklist, the EU’s 27 member states found a compromise that meant delisting the two oligarchs in spite of very few countries wanting this outcome. EU sanctions have to be approved unanimously. Continue reading...

Sources: BBC News, Deutsche Welle, The Guardian

item.title: Six-year-old sets Rubik’s Cube world record twice in three days
item.description:
Lian Yunzhi solves 3x3 puzzle on several occasions in average time of under 4.5 seconds, according to state media A six-year-old Chinese girl has set a new women’s world record for solving a Rubik’s Cube in just over four seconds, state media reported. “Speedcuber” Lian Yunzhi broke the women’s 3x3 average world record twice this month at two World Cube Association certified competitions in Wuhan and Guangzhou, according to state broadcaster CCTV on Monday.
